body: United Airlines is accelerating a fleet modernization that will soon make its Airbus A320s a rare sight in its livery. According to Planespotters.net, cited by Simple Flying, the carrier has 59 A320-200s in service and two parked, with an average age of 26.7 years, making them among the oldest active Airbus narrowbodies in the mainline fleet. Once a reliable staple of the domestic network, the A320ceo family is now showing its age against rising fuel costs, maintenance demands and heightened customer expectations.

The economics are stark. Chief executive Scott Kirby told ch-aviation that United spent $100 million on engine work in 2024 alone, prompting the decision to retire 21 aircraft in 2025. As reported by ch-aviation, United earmarked at least 17 of its oldest A320s for retirement between August and October of 2025. Every dollar spent keeping a 30-year-old A320 flying is a dollar not invested in a fuel-efficient, higher-capacity replacement, and as the A321neo order stream accelerates, keeping the older aircraft makes less and less financial sense.

The A321neo is the replacement. It offers a significant reduction in cost per available seat mile compared with the A320ceo, thanks to new-generation LEAP-1A engines, aerodynamic improvements and lighter materials, and it carries 25 to 30 percent more passengers in United's configuration while burning less fuel per seat. United has ordered 130 A321neos and 50 A321XLRs, and the A321neo is already viewed by the airline as its top domestic performer. The same type is also set to replace much of the Boeing 757's capacity: Planespotters.net lists 36 757-200s at an average age of 29.8 years and 19 757-300s at 24.3 years in service at United.

Retirements will be phased rather than overnight, aligning with deliveries so routes remain fully served, and delays to the A321XLR mean the transition will unfold in stages. For passengers, the shift promises a more consistent onboard product, with modern cabins, larger overhead bins, fast WiFi and seat-back entertainment on most A321neo configurations. Ultimately, the retirement of the A320ceo fleet is a strategic step toward a more unified, efficient and passenger-friendly United, with the A321neo, the 737 MAX and the 787 Dreamliner defining the airline's flying experience well into the 2030s.
en.summary: United's Airbus A320s average 26.7 years old, and with $100 million spent on engine work in 2024 alone, the airline is phasing them out in favour of the A321neo, which carries 25 to 30 percent more passengers at lower fuel burn per seat.
en.title: Why United Airlines doesn't want its Airbus A320s anymore

body: 美聯航正在加速機隊現代化，不久後空中巴士A320將很少再披著美聯航塗裝出現。據Simple Flying引述Planespotters.net的資料，美聯航現役A320-200共有59架、另有2架停場，平均機齡26.7年，是其幹線機隊中最老的一批空中巴士窄體機。A320ceo系列曾是美國國內航線的可靠主力，如今在燃油成本上升、維修需求增加與旅客期待提高的背景下，已顯老態。
經濟帳很清楚。執行長柯比向ch-aviation表示，美聯航僅2024年就在發動機維修上花了1億美元，促使公司決定在2025年退役21架飛機。據ch-aviation報導，美聯航已把至少17架最老的A320排定於2025年8月至10月退役。讓一架30年機齡的A320繼續飛行所花的每一塊錢，都是無法投入更省油、載客量更大的替代機型的錢；隨著A321neo交付加速，保留這些老飛機愈來愈不划算。

接班的是A321neo。與A320ceo相比，A321neo每可用座位英里的成本大幅降低，受惠於新一代LEAP-1A發動機、氣動改良與更輕的材料；在美聯航的布局下，A321neo載客量多出25%至30%，每座位油耗卻更低。美聯航已訂購130架A321neo與50架A321XLR，而A321neo在美聯航眼中已是國內線表現最好的機型。同一機型也將接替波音757的大部分運能：Planespotters.net資料顯示，美聯航現役757-200有36架、平均機齡29.8年，757-300有19架、平均機齡24.3年。

退役將分階段進行、配合新機交付，讓航線維持服務不中斷；A321XLR交付有所延誤，也使轉換必須逐步推進。對旅客而言，這波換裝意味著更一致的機上產品：A321neo多數布局配備現代客艙、更大的Airspace XL行李艙、全彩LED情境燈、高速無線網路與座椅後方娛樂系統。整體而言，A320ceo退役是美聯航邁向更統一、高效且旅客友善營運的策略一步，A321neo、737 MAX與787夢幻客機將共同形塑該公司直至2030年代的飛行體驗。
zh.summary: 美聯航A320機隊平均機齡26.7年，僅2024年發動機維修就花了1億美元，公司正以A321neo逐步取代，後者載客量多25%至30%、每座位油耗更低。
zh.title: 美聯航為何不再要A320：機齡近27年的飛機讓位給A321neo
